parties.counterparty: Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI" — site developer/host, vendor side)

plans.note: No liability/limitation heading surfaced in the outline; this looks like a short intra-group development and hosting agreement. Scan the unnumbered body of sec-p0001 (Articles after 1.x, especially any 'Liability'/'Disclaimer' text preceding the signature block at sec-p0072) for a cap, consequential-damages waiver or one-sided exclusion in HDI's favour before concluding it is missing.

Rule expects a vendor indemnity (third-party IP infringement in the site/software HDI develops and hosts, plus HDI misconduct). No indemnity heading appears in the outline; check the closing articles of sec-p0001 near sec-p0072 for any indemnity, and note whether the only indemnity runs from the Company to HDI.

Look in the Article 1 services/scope paragraphs (sec-1.4 and its siblings) for any restriction on the Company operating other web sites, selling Deerskin Products through other channels, or building its own site. Likely absent, but the 'Deerskin Products' definition makes a channel restriction plausible.

Hosting/development agreements of this type commonly appoint HDI as sole and exclusive developer/host of the Company's site. Check the Article 1 scope paragraphs around sec-1.4 for 'sole', 'exclusive' or 'shall not engage any other' language binding us, and confirm whether we retain freedom to use other hosts/suppliers.

Check any fees/pricing article in sec-p0001 for most-favoured-customer wording. Only a provision obliging the Company to give HDI its best terms is a deviation; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and should not be flagged.

Article 5 deals with personnel/representatives (sec-5.4 appoints each party's representative), so any employee non-solicit would most likely sit in the paragraphs around sec-5.4. Verify duration, scope and whether a general-advertising carve-out exists before treating as absent.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms a term/termination provision exists in the unnumbered portion of sec-p0001. Locate it and test whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty and whether HDI has a mirror-image or broader mid-term walk-away right.

Same term/termination article as T4C ('Termination Date'). Check for automatic renewal, the length of the non-renewal notice window and any renewal price uplift; a missing uplift cap is a rationale note, not a separate deviation.

Expect a miscellaneous/general article immediately before the signature block at sec-p0072. Confirm governing law is NY, DE, CA or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration; New York is likely given HDI's profile.

Search the same miscellaneous article near sec-p0072 (the 'Time of Receipt' definition points to a notices clause in that group). Confirm the Company may assign to affiliates and successors and that HDI has no termination right on our change of control — relevant here since the parties are affiliated and the Company may be sold.

Core rule for a site development deal: check who owns the developed site, content, software and the customer/transaction data. sec-1.4 (HDI providing the Company with access to ...) is the likely data/records hook; look for any grant or assignment of Company IP, 'Deerskin Products' marks or customer data to HDI.

Identify the licence direction first: a licence to the Company to use HDI's site/platform (test affiliate and contractor coverage and any 'revocable at will' wording) versus a trademark licence we grant HDI in the 'Deerskin Products' marks, which is outbound and not flagged under this rule.
Check any fees/records paragraphs in sec-p0001 for HDI inspection rights over the Company's books, systems or usage; if the only audit right runs in our favour (records of hosting fees), do not flag.

Look in the fees and termination paragraphs of sec-p0001 for early-termination fees, penalties or stipulated damages payable by the Company. Service credits or remedies flowing to us are welcome and should not be flagged.

Check the Article 1 services paragraphs (around sec-1.4) for performance standards/service levels and the closing articles for any 'AS IS'/warranty disclaimer by HDI. Report as missing only if there is neither a performance warranty nor a re-performance remedy anywhere.

HDI hosts our site and handles customer data, so the rule applies. No insurance heading appears in the outline; confirm by scanning the general/miscellaneous paragraphs of sec-p0001 before recording as missing.

Check the fees/compensation paragraphs of sec-p0001 for minimum purchase, minimum volume or take-or-pay obligations on the Company; a fixed monthly hosting fee alone is not a take-or-pay and should be noted rather than flagged.

Test the effects-of-termination paragraphs tied to the 'Termination Date' definition, together with sec-1.4 (Company access rights), for return of customer/transaction data, transfer of the site and domain, and wind-down assistance; flag as missing if only access during the term is addressed.
